rubric.90-100: Exceptional national or international destination with outstanding independent depth.
rubric.80-89: Strong destination supporting a substantial day visit through several independent draws and practical provision.
rubric.70-79: Worth a visit, with enough independent attractions, character, trails and services for a planned half or full day.
rubric.60-69: Notable stop with multiple independent reasons to visit and adequate practical provision.
rubric.50-59: Strong character or a focused draw, but insufficient independent depth for the main town map.
rubric.35-49: Recognisable village or hamlet with modest independent interest.
rubric.20-34: Minor locality, estate or district with limited public visitor value.
rubric.0-19: Named property or dispersed locality without a verified public settlement experience.

rules: The score is assessed before the 60-point map threshold is applied.
Standalone attractions remain under See and cannot substitute for settlement merit.
A score review does not falsely claim completion of the separate See, Eat, trails, parking, toilets, picnic, accessibility and heritage content audit.
Existing dog-access ratings remain separate and produce the dog-owner score adjustment.

results.name: East Haven
results.rationale: A genuinely worthwhile small coastal village: an award-winning beach, distinctive fishing-community heritage, community gardens, a strong coastal route and unusually complete practical facilities. Its limited scale, seasonal toilets, very small car park and lack of café keep it in the 60–69 band.

results.name: Panbride
results.rationale: Panbride has a rewarding churchyard group and Craigmill Den on a verified council walk, but it remains a very small hamlet without a café, public toilet, picnic facility or dedicated visitor car park. These attractions support a worthwhile local detour, not a 60+ town destination.
